questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go far away from home and experience a high level university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine, I also knew a few people who had been on exchange in Singapore who were able to provide some information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a student office and they were also easy to get in touch with via email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of housing options. Most of these with your own room but shared kitchen and bathroom. Some of the houses also provided a meal plan. Also note that many of the options do not have aircondition - so I bought my own portable one.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of cheap option on campus. Easy to get a meal that was like 5-8 SGD. I almost didnt cook while I was there - because you had to buy all the kitchen utensils such as pans, plates, cutlery etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would choose on campus housing over off campus because you meet so many other students, and this is here where everything is happening. However, be aware of the non-airconditioning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only thing I was not satisfied with is that the facility where I lived was pretty worn down - i lived in PGPR. However, considering the price for rent it was totally fair. I paid approximately 14.000 DKK for the entire stay.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite a long process with many documents to send and fill out etc. But worth it!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could ask both KU and the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about the classes - it's possible to swap them once you are there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very insightful and very talented professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took classes that where the level 4000.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's more of a lecture style and not as much with participation from the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Commercial Arbitration, Trade Finance Law, Multinational Enterprises and International Law, Environmental Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
It's a good idea to take one intensive course (the 4 units ones), because the classes are done after three weeks so you have more time in the end of the semester. I really loved the course International Commercial Arbitration - however, it involved an oral moot exercise as part of the grade (40%) and it is quite demanding in terms of work load. But I loved it.

Can also recommend Environmental Law - I chose one topic for my exam essay and just wrote about this.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Bying stuff for my room - the AC, pillow, sheets, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The AC was a little expensive. Public transportation and food was less expensive than expected. And also the on campus housing, very cheap. Budget wise cannot recommend living off campus - it's super expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was many sports clubs, events and things to do.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of sports, concerts, film club etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attend the events for exchange students (there will be one big whatsapp group), and you will get a lot of friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel. Flight tickets are cheap and there are endless destinations to explore in South East Asia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not to difficult - although it is Asia, it is also a quite Western and modern country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There' s a lot of silly rules to get used to, but it's nothing serious.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people, so kind. And the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get on campus accommodation, attend the activities you find interesting, and prepare yourself for the humidity.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends, being on my own, taking high level classes.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far away from home and getting settled and start a new everyday life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
